answer: Agents can earn voting weight only through a time-locked stake that is slashed when a randomly audited task fails. Splitting one identity into a nebula of aliases does not multiply weight: each vote is capped by the stake actually locked, and each alias requires separate capital. To sway a decision, an attacker must therefore immobilize funds and risk losing them, while honest agents build reputation through repeated work. The pigment of identity is cheap; the cost of credible influence can reach a nadir only if the attacker accepts real, forfeitable exposure.
